st: Pat the beef dry and season it with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, about [[5 minutes]] per batch. Move the beef to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 8 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until the mixture turns thick and darker.
Whisk the peanut butter with [[1 cup]] of the water until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Return the beef to the pot, add the remaining water and the whole chili, and bring to a gentle boil. Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes.
Add the sweet potatoes, cover again, and simmer for 20 minutes until the beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir now and then so the peanut sauce does not stick. If it is too thick, add a splash of water.
Taste and add salt if needed. Remove the whole chili and serve hot with rice.
Season the beef with half of the salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef well on all sides, about 8 minutes, then remove it.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 5 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and oily at the edges.
Return the beef to the pot, add [[1 cup]] of the broth and the bay leaf, cover, and simmer on low for 40 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the carrots and cabbage and simmer for 10 more minutes. Lift the meat and vegetables out onto a plate and keep them warm.
Measure the sauce left in the pot and add broth to make [[3.5 cups]] of liquid. Bring to a boil and add the remaining salt.
Stir in the rinsed rice, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the rice steam for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the rice on a big platter topped with the meat and vegetables.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Add [[2 cups]] of the water, the okra, the baobab powder and half of the salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the okra is tender and the sauce is slightly slippery. Keep warm.
For the tô, bring [[3 cups]] of the water to a boil in a separate heavy pot with the remaining salt.
Whisk [[1 cup]] of the flour with [[1 cup]] of cold water until it is a smooth paste with no lumps.
Pour the paste into the boiling water, whisking, and cook for 5 minutes until it thickens into a thin porridge.
Lower the heat. Add the remaining [[1 cup]] flour a little at a time, stirring hard with a sturdy wooden spoon, until a stiff, smooth dough forms.
Cover and cook on low for 5 minutes, then stir and press the dough against the pot to remove lumps.
Scoop the tô into wet bowls and shape into smooth domes. Serve warm with the okra sauce poured around it.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb for about 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and chili for 1 minute, then add the water.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the lamb is tender.
If using frozen jute leaves, thaw them. Chop fresh leaves finely.
Add the leaves and the smoked fish to the pot and stir well.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the leaves are soft and the sauce is thick and slippery.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with rice or tô.
In a large bowl, combine the onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] of the oil, half the salt and the pepper.
Add the chicken, rub the marinade over it, cover, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, shaking off the onions. Keep the onions and liquid.
Heat the oven broiler or a grill. Cook the chicken for about 6 minutes per side until browned and charred in spots.
Heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the marinated onions with the leftover marinade for 15 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Add the water, bay leaf, chili and remaining salt, then add the browned chicken.
Cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes, turning the chicken once, until the thickest piece reaches 165°F (74°C).
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed. Serve over rice.

ing: or any firm white fish, cut into large pieces
st: Rub the fish with the lemon juice, half of the salt and the pepper. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the fish for 2 minutes per side. Set it aside.
Heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and chili for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and tomato paste.
Cook for 12 minutes, stirring and mashing, until the sauce is thick and the oil rises to the top.
Pour in the water and the remaining salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Lay the fish in the sauce, spooning some over the top. Cover and simmer gently for 8 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Serve with rice or fried plantains.
Season the beef with half of the salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 8 minutes total. Remove it.
Cook the onions in the pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Return the beef to the pot, add [[3 cups]] of the broth and the chili, and simmer covered on low for 45 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with [[1 cup]] of the hot broth from the pot until smooth, then stir it back in.
Add the carrots and the remaining broth, plus the remaining salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage wedges, cover, and simmer 15 more minutes until the vegetables and beef are tender.
The sauce should be thick, with a little orange oil on top. Serve over rice.

ing: peeled, woody core removed, cut into chunks
st: Put the cassava and plantains in a large pot, cover with water, and add half of the salt.
Boil for 25 minutes until both are very soft when pierced with a fork.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter into the water, pour it into the tomato pot, add the remaining salt, and simmer for 10 minutes. Keep warm.
Drain the cassava and plantains, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Mash them in a large bowl with a potato masher or pound with a wooden pestle until smooth and stretchy. Add a spoonful of cooking water if dry.
With wet hands, shape the dough into four smooth balls.
Serve each ball in a bowl with the peanut sauce poured around it.
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl.
Bring the water to a boil and pour it over the couscous. Cover and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Fluff the grains with a fork and spread them on a plate to cool for 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the yogurt, sugar, milk, vanilla and nutmeg until smooth.
Break up any clumps in the couscous, then fold it into the yogurt mixture.
Chill for at least 30 minutes if you like it cold. Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Serve in small bowls, cold or at room temperature.
Rinse the hibiscus flowers quickly under cold water.
Bring [[6 cups]] of the water to a boil in a pot.
Add the flowers and ginger, turn off the heat, cover, and steep for 20 minutes.
Strain into a pitcher, pressing the flowers to get out all the liquid.
Stir in the sugar while still warm until dissolved.
Add the mint, vanilla, lime juice and the remaining [[2 cups]] cold water.
Chill for at least 2 hours. Serve over ice with mint leaves.
